To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) low frequencies of T cells eliciting by aerosol Mtb infection recognize viable Mtb-inflected macrophages; (2) BCG-vaccinated mice have low frequencies of Mtb-infected cell-recognizing T cells; and (3) CD4 T cells recognize Mbt-infected macrophage more frequently than CD8 T cells.

(1) T cells elicited in response to Mtb infection or BCG vaccination recognize Mtb-inflected macrophages, but at low frequencies; (2) T cells eliciting by Mtb infection are classically MHC-restricted; (3) CD8 T cells are less efficient than CD4 T cells at recognizing Mtb-infected cells; (4) CD4 T cells from the lung are more sensitive than those from the spleen at recognizing Mtb infection; and
a relatively small proportion of T cells from the lung and spleen of infected mice recognize Mtb-inflected macrophages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new assay to assess the ability of T cells to respond to Mtb-infected cells.
the immune response to the tuberculosis bacterium Mycobacterium Tuberculosis (Mtb), and the development of new tuberculosis vaccines.
the development of novel approaches to measure immune responses to Mycobacterium Tuberculosis.

the majority of CD4 and CD7 T cells elicited in the lung by Mtb infection are not able to recognize infected macrophage cells.

Mtb-specific T-cells from the lungs of Mtb-infected C57BL/10 mice recognize infected macrophage targets with frequencies comparable to those determined using other methods, including intracellular cytokine analysis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of T cell responses elicited by M. tuberculosis (Mtb), or M. bovis Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG), are not specific for infected cells.

the frequency of CD4 and CD 8 T cells that recognize mycobacteria-infected macrophage in the lungs of infected or vaccinated mice is low, and that these cells may be important for protective immunity against mycobacteria.

the frequency of CD8+ T cells recognizing Mtb-infected APCs is higher than previously reported, and the frequency of T-cells recognizing Mtb-infecetd APCs is lower than the frequency of T cell responses to Mtb antigenic peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency of Mtb-infected-macrophage-specific T cells is low in the lungs of mice infected with Mtb.
the frequency of CD4 and CD 8 T cells that recognize Mycobacterium-infected macrophage is relatively low in the lungs of Mtb-infected mice.
the majority of T cells eliciting by infection or vaccination with BCG do not recognize infected macrophage.
